  • Reddit boasts engagement metrics that would be the envy of many other online platforms: Over 80% of its monetization comes from loyal, logged-in users, who spend eight times as much time on the site in their fifth year as they did in their first.And yet, Reddit’s share price is down 62% for the year to date, as the platform grapples with an internet increasingly shaped by AI.In its Q3 earnings call in October, Reddit’s CEO, Steve Huffman, noted Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode were leading to a decline in search referrals to the site, the lifeblood of many social and media-adjacent businesses.
  • It has been revealed that chief Operating Officer Jen Wong told Fortune in an exclusive interview that some factors were lost in translation.
  • Sources indicate that in their first year on Reddit, users tend to spend five minutes a day on the app or website.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Reddit boasts engagement metrics that would be the envy of many other online platforms: Over 80% of its monetization comes from loyal, logged-in users, who spend eight times as much time on the site in their fifth year as they did in their first.And yet, Reddit’s share price is down 62% for the year to date, as the platform grapples with an internet increasingly shaped by AI.In its Q3 earnings call in October, Reddit’s CEO, Steve Huffman, noted Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode were leading to a decline in search referrals to the site, the lifeblood of many social and media-adjacent businesses. The market did not like the implications, and the share price dropped from just shy of $130 apiece to a little under $91 overnight.

It has been revealed that chief Operating Officer Jen Wong told Fortune in an exclusive interview that some factors were lost in translation. The shifting relationship between Reddit and search engines “requires a different kind of partnership,” she remarked, rather than any separation. If anything, Wong believes Reddit is well-positioned to navigate the new era of online information gathering.

Sources indicate that in their first year on Reddit, users tend to spend five minutes a day on the app or website. By their fifth year, that figure rises to 40 minutes, Wong tells Fortune. The number of “communities” (topic-focused discussion groups) that users are in jumps from 10 in the first year to more than 100 by their fifth.

Recent findings suggest that “Reddit is really interesting because we have users who have over a decade of karma,” Wong remarked. “Reddit typically gets you as a young adult, and then you season over time in this incredible way. If you look at the chart, it’s very consistent.”.

According to recent reports, wong sees people’ changing life stages reflected in the communities they join: “[They’ve] gone through life with Reddit. You started as a student, you got your first rental place, you got married, you had kids, and we see kind of your life’s journey.

“You just never age out of Reddit because all of those life stages are available to you on Reddit, and you’re always going through something that you have to traverse.”.

Sources indicate that navigating different life stages appears to be a key differentiator of the Reddit platform. In 2024, an article published in “Higher Education Research and Development” found that one in three students use Reddit for study help, ahead of TikTok at 14.9% and Instagram at 12.7%. YouTube leads the pack, with more than 90% of the 1,000 students surveyed using it for educational purposes.

The site’s leadership wants to expand on that function. In early November, Reddit launched Reddit Reviews, organizing product feedback across multiple communities to provide overall ratings.

“Logged-in users season very, very well, which is another motivation for us to say we want more logged-in users, because we want the opportunity to teach you about all these other aspects of Reddit,” Wong adds, “Not just the information and retrieval part of Reddit, but the part of Reddit that is around the connection, the communities, and the conversation.”.

Every media platform needs to maintain or grow its audience. But Reddit has a unique problem: It has more than 100,000 “communities,” according to various reports, all of which have volunteer moderators. These moderators are unpaid and are not Reddit employees, instead choosing to spend their free time building their communities and ensuring the content is fit for its purpose.

But with ever-evolving channels and fresh voices within them, demand for experienced moderators is high—in fact, Reddit even has a dedicated page where communities can recruit volunteer moderators.

In the recruitment group, individuals are either looking for or offering moderation skills for hours a day, on a daily basis. Posts include requests for moderators in specific time zones, often for about 3 hours a day.

It has been revealed that but Wong says even if Reddit wanted to bring its moderators in-house and pay them, they probably wouldn’t take it. While moderators are interested in earning, she said, they didn’t want strings attached: “They really like their independence from us, to be able to say, ‘This is our community, we set the rules, and this is how we want to operate.’.

“Our relationship with moderators, I think, has greatly improved. I’ve been with Reddit eight, almost nine years, and where at the beginning we were not investing as much as we could in creating moderator tools and making their lives better in terms of reducing some of the repetitive work, over the last few years we’ve done a much better job also applying AI to help them with a toolkit, so that they can spend the time on the things that they really care about.”.

But overall, Wong is bullish on Reddit’s long-term position in the age of AI. “Reddit is basically the taste layer of the internet. No model and no recommendation system can be good, I think, without a dash of Reddit in it, because you just don’t have the freshness of information. That adds value in so many places.”.

#202211. Clock Ticking on Zcash’s Sprout Pool: 22,263 ZEC Unmoved Ahead of NU7 Lock

Clock Ticking on Zcash’s Sprout Pool: 22,263 ZEC Unmoved Ahead of NU7 Lock

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1224 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, daily pool data shows Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped.
  • Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.
  • Most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

In a recent development, daily pool data shows Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped. The last withdrawal was on October 19.

Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.

Most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC. That number is accurate, but it is a single snapshot. It doesn't show whether the people who own those coins are doing anything about the deadline.

We checked the pool every day, and the answer so far is no.

Sources indicate that according to ZecStats' daily value-pool records, Sprout has held exactly 22,263.34162335 ZEC since October 19. That is 11 straight days, and more than 12,000 blocks, without a single zatoshi leaving the pool. Our October 25 piece recorded the drop from 22,309 ZEC to 22,263 ZEC. Since then the balance hasn't moved.

It has been revealed that zecStats publishes a daily CSV of every Zcash value pool, using the last block of each UTC day. Its figures follow the valuePools field that a full node returns through the getblockchaininfo call. The archive starts on July 30, 2026, and gives a 92-day picture of the Sprout pool.

Recent findings suggest that across those 92 days, about 374 ZEC, or 1.65% of the pool, left Sprout. That is an average of roughly 4 ZEC a day. The average hides the real pattern, though: the pool moved on only 15 of the 92 days.

Most of the withdrawals came in a few large transfers in September:.

It has been revealed that together with smaller moves on August 31, September 17 and September 19, the 30 days to September 29 saw 310.5 ZEC leave Sprout. That is about 10 ZEC a day.

October was much quieter. Apart from one withdrawal of 46.05 ZEC on October 19, the month's activity was small change:.

Since October 19, there has been no movement at all.

At September's pace, about 70 ZEC more would leave before activation. At October's pace, it would be well under 15 ZEC. On the last 11 days' pace, the answer is zero.

The deadline is set in ZIP 259, which defines how the NU7 network upgrade is deployed. It sets the mainnet activation height at 3,543,405.

NU7 does not introduce a latest transaction format. Instead, after activation, version 4 transactions become invalid, while versions 5 and 6 remain valid. Sprout's design is the problem. As ZIP 259 puts it: "Because Sprout transfers can only be represented by version 4 transactions, funds remaining in the Sprout pool become unspendable.".

In a recent development, the coins would not be destroyed, and NU7 does not change Zcash's supply cap. They would simply be stuck in a pool that no valid transaction can spend from. Today the stranded amount would be 22,263 ZEC, about 0.13% of the roughly 17.01 million ZEC in circulation.

The rest of the upgrade is larger:.

Industry observers note that ZIP 259 also skips Zcash's usual three-month gap between the first supporting software release and activation. Operators running unsupported software could stay online and follow a pre-NU7 chain.

According to recent reports, as of ZecStats' latest upgrade on October 30 at 13:09 UTC, the chain was at block 3,535,877. That leaves 7,528 blocks until activation.

In October, the network averaged about 1,147 blocks a day, or one roughly every 75.3 seconds. At that rate, block 3,543,405 arrives around 02:00–03:00 UTC on November 6. That is the evening of November 5 in the Americas and the early hours of November 6 in Europe and Africa.

It has been revealed that small changes in block times could move that window by a few hours. Holders who strategy to move funds on the final day risk missing the cutoff.

It has been revealed that in practice, getting funds out of Sprout means sending a version 4 transaction that moves them into a newer pool before activation. Customers need software that can still build Sprout transactions and a synced node or wallet that recognizes their old notes.

The September withdrawals show that some holders are still paying attention. Several were round amounts, such as 99.998 ZEC, which is consistent with someone moving 100 ZEC and paying a fee. The 11-day pause since October 19 suggests something else: most of the remaining 22,263 ZEC may belong to keys that are lost, forgotten or no longer used.

Sources indicate that that has been part of the debate about Sprout for years. A pool that has been shrinking slowly since Zcash's early days is now on a fixed timetable. The daily data indicates that most of its remaining balance is not being moved.

It has been revealed that every report that cites "about 22,000 ZEC at risk" is technically correct. The more useful figure for anyone tracking the upgrade is the rate of change, and right now that rate is zero.

It has been revealed that the useful thing to watch over the next week is whether the Sprout line in ZecStats' daily data moves again before block 3,543,405. If it doesn't, Zcash will activate NU7 with about 22,263 ZEC permanently locked in its first shielded pool. That would be one of the largest deliberate freezes of user funds by any major blockchain upgrade, and nearly all of it would be coins whose owners did not move them in time.

Former Mt. Gox CEO Warns Pump.fun Consumers Their Private Keys Are at Risk

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gox CEO Mark Karpelès has strongly warned users of Solana-based memecoin launchpad Pump.fun about potential major security risks associated with the new wallet migration process, which could put users' private keys at great risk.
  • Sources indicate that karpelès’ warning comes as Pump.fun has set a Nov.
  • In a recent development, but to maintain their current accounts, Pump.fun is asking consumers to import their private keys.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that former Mt. Gox CEO Mark Karpelès has strongly warned users of Solana-based memecoin launchpad Pump.fun about potential major security risks associated with the new wallet migration process, which could put users' private keys at great risk.

Sources indicate that karpelès’ warning comes as Pump.fun has set a Nov. 30 deadline to stop allowing external wallet logins to its website. The platform is moving to email and social logins, which will enable users to access their accounts via Google, Apple and GitHub.

In a recent development, but to maintain their current accounts, Pump.fun is asking consumers to import their private keys. This is what Karpelès thinks could compromise the security of their crypto assets.

In a recent X post, Karpelès said he studied Pump.fun's JavaScript code to understand the nature of the newly introduced migration process.

The analysis has raised questions about the security of users’ private keys, despite the platform's claims.

“At best, it's a misnomer to refer to it as 'end-to-end encryption,'” noted Karpelès.

According to Karpelès, users' private keys are first encrypted in their browsers before being sent through Pump.fun’s servers to the platform’s wallet infrastructure provider, Privy.

Sources indicate that also, Pump.fun's backend provides the public key used for encryption during migration. Users’ browsers have no way to check whether the public key is authentic, according to Karpelès.

The possibility of a security breach involving Privy’s infrastructure is another major concern.

“Your money also now relies on Privy never getting hacked,” Karpelès warned.

One of the most important aspects of Karpelès' warning is the need for migration in the first place.

He said Pump.fun could use signature-based authentication without forcing owners to expose their private keys.

Pump.fun already uses a "Sign in with Solana" message to prove ownership of a wallet, according to Karpelès.

So theoretically, customers can prove ownership of their wallets and execute transactions without having to import their private credentials into a latest system.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson believes the network is far from reaching its full potential, arguing that a single successful application could completely transform market sentiment and attract millions of new people.

In a recent development, as pointed out by Cardanians, Hoskinson stressed that market narratives can change promptly, stating, “Facts and circumstances change. It takes just one viral application to bring millions of people in and change the narrative and tone of everything.”.

It has been revealed that he reinforced his confidence in the ecosystem, declaring, “ADA’s not done. Cardano’s not done.”.

Interestingly, Hoskinson recently noted that Cardano was entering a new phase, with priorities shifting from building blockchain infrastructure toward developing products that encourage meaningful adoption. He acknowledged that Cardano’s Midnight network would take the driver’s seat in this transition.

In a recent development, what’s Cardano’s bigger picture? Hoskinson seems to acknowledge that turning capabilities into applications that attract users and deliver practical value should receive close attention.

Cardano is also demonstrating its potential through real-world deployments. The Cardano Foundation recently highlighted an initiative in India where police are using the blockchain to track and preserve evidence throughout criminal investigations.

Living Computers closed, but its spirit and vintage machines live on at a museum south of Seattle

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1782 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 24, 2026 at 11:08 amNovember 25, 2026 at 8:16 am.
  • When Seattle’s Living Computers: Museum + Labs closed for good in 2024, it seemed like the end of the line for anyone who wanted to do more than just look at old computers.
  • But in a Tukwila business park 20 minutes south of downtown, a sizable collection of vintage computers is still alive — kept running by a few of the same people who once did the same for Paul Allen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 24, 2026 at 11:08 amNovember 25, 2026 at 8:16 am.

When Seattle’s Living Computers: Museum + Labs closed for good in 2024, it seemed like the end of the line for anyone who wanted to do more than just look at old computers.

But in a Tukwila business park 20 minutes south of downtown, a sizable collection of vintage computers is still alive — kept running by a few of the same people who once did the same for Paul Allen.

The Interim Computer Museum is a nonprofit that opened to the public in 2024 and has quietly grown into a hands-on showcase of dozens of machines, from early Apples and IBM PCs to hulking DEC systems that once filled university labs. At 4,400 square feet of public space, it’s nearly as significant as Living Computers was before that museum expanded in 2016.

ICM is led by Stephen Jones, who calls himself the museum’s “caretaker.” Jones spent two decades helping track down and restore machines for Allen, first at PDP Planet, Allen’s private collection of vintage systems, then at Living Computers, where he was senior engineering manager.

When the late Microsoft co-founder’s estate wound down Living Computers, the majority of the collection went to the Mimms Museum of Technology and Art in Georgia, where Jones is also a curator. The machines in Tukwila are privately owned, and Jones has helped bankroll ICM with personal funds, with plans to eventually donate the collection to the nonprofit.

The Mimms museum now holds the Living Computers trademark and has granted ICM “legacy use” of the name, but Jones stated he didn’t want to revive it as ICM’s own because “it has a finite past.” Instead, he wants to carry on “the spirit of the engineering focus.”.

“Between Mimms and here, this is the legacy,” Jones stated. “We show the name and the connection to the past, but we’re doing upcoming things.”.

Sources indicate that ICM occupies space in Seattle Exchange @ Southcenter, a sprawl of low-slung flex buildings off Strander Boulevard near Westfield Southcenter mall. Its neighbors include a car detailer, a pest control company, a welding shop, an embroiderer and an upholsterer.

More than four decades ago, Seattle Computer Products operated just down Industry Drive. That’s where Tim Paterson wrote 86-DOS, the operating system Microsoft bought and turned into MS-DOS for IBM’s first PC.

Jones calls that proximity part of the “magic” of the location. The museum has a Gazelle computer that SCP built nearby, using boards that Jones said the company hired high school students to assemble and test. Volunteers recently pulled data off its hard drive, which boots into MS-DOS 2.11 and still holds SCP’s own source code.

In a recent development, allen’s fingerprints are everywhere. One display holds a 1971 letter from Hellmut Golde, director of the University of Washington’s Computer Science Laboratory, kicking Allen and his “friends from the Lakeside School” out of the lab. Among the offenses: tying up the teletypes to print “endless listings,” and taking an acoustic coupler from a professor’s office “without leaving at least a note.” Golde asked them to turn in their keys.

The letter sits beside an Imlac PDS-1, the same type of graphics computer Golde scolded the teens for using without permission. More than five decades later, the letter is headed back to campus: ICM looks to display it, along with the Imlac, at UW’s 60th anniversary celebration for its computer science program in March.

In a recent development, jones recalled that Allen insisted visitors to Living Computers get “the 10-minute experience” of loading an Altair 8800 from paper tape, just as he remembered it. The kit computer was the machine for which Allen and Bill Gates wrote Microsoft’s first product, and Allen wanted to reinforce “how far we’ve come and how difficult old computers were.” ICM has an Altair 8800 on display.

Industry observers note that around the corner is Miss Piggy, a DEC datasystem 570 that Microsoft used in the early 1980s to support the group that built Multiplan, Word and later Excel. It was also the email host for much of the tech giant, including Gates, who once had to print out an vital message on its console printer when the system went down before a speaking engagement.

Recent findings suggest that recovered email demonstrates Allen pushing to get Piggy networked. “Paul Allen is very keen on doing this,” Henry Burgess wrote in 1982. Retired in 1986, the machine now runs again in Tukwila. It’s one of ICM’s most popular remote systems, and some fans come in just to write programs while sitting next to it.

Other local ties include a PDP-7 that Boeing used to process flight data in the 1960s, and a Toad-1, a modern take on the PDP-10 built in the 1990s by Redmond’s XKL. Jones first got involved with Allen’s world through a 1997 Usenet post inviting PDP-10 enthusiasts onto a Toad. That machine became the cornerstone of PDP Planet.

In a 2024 video for Christie’s, Jones stated what inspired Allen was “being able to recover old programs, mythical code, and get them running on hardware so that they can be studied.”.

Industry observers note that asked what Allen would make of ICM, Jones didn’t hesitate. “I think he’d be happy,” he noted.

On a monitor beside ICM’s PDP-6, a 1968 artificial intelligence program is having trouble.

“SORRY, I DON’T KNOW THE WORD ‘STEEPLE,'” it replies.

According to recent reports, the program is SHRDLU, created by Terry Winograd at the MIT AI Lab. It let a user type plain-English commands to move blocks around a virtual world. Only the PDP-6’s front console and display survived, so ICM is rebuilding the machine as a “hybrid,” with the original hardware wired to an emulator.

Jones sees a lesson in that old error message. “You look at this and you think of how we use ChatGPT now,” he stated. “The cool thing about SHRDLU is that it can tell you ‘I don’t know.’ It doesn’t try to fabricate anything.”.

ICM has its own ties to the modern AI world. An Anthropic employee is a member and strong supporter, and in October the museum brought six vintage computing stations to an Anthropic event, where the manufacturer’s Claude chatbot wrote programs for machines like the Commodore 64.

Back in Tukwila, Claude has become one of ICM’s most useful restoration tools. The team feeds it huge stacks of scanned documentation, such as the full set of schematics for a PDP-10. When a machine has a logic fault, they ask where to look, and Claude points them to a page in the maintenance manual or a likely bad module.

“That’s turned things that would take a couple of weeks to solve into a couple of days,” Jones remarked.

AI can point the way, but the repairs remain hands-on work. When Miss Piggy wouldn’t run properly this year, former Living Computers engineer Josh Dersch stepped through the machine’s microcode one instruction at a time using a recreated DEC test board, until he found a single bad chip. A spare board brought it back.

In a recent development, asked if it still takes a human to keep these machines running, Jones agreed — at least for now. If a humanoid robot with AI built in ever demonstrates up to do the repairs, he joked, “then I sit at the front desk all day.”.

Nearly everything at ICM is meant to be touched, switched on and played with, and that can be intimidating. On machines with nothing but a text prompt, “you kind of have to know the commands in your head already,” Jones said.

That’s by design. From the start, the idea was to challenge people “either by confronting them with their past or demonstrating how difficult it was,” Jones noted. His example: two friends, one with an Apple IIe and one with an IBM PC, whose computers “could never share” software. ICM continues that legacy, he said, “challenging the visitor to go beyond what they might feel comfortable with.”.

It has been revealed that volunteers have written cheat sheets to help newcomers, and Jones is encouraged when families come in and kids start typing BASIC programs. “That to me was the spirit of what PDP Planet and Living Computers was meant to be,” he noted.

Very little is behind glass. Jones jokes that a Timex Sinclair 1000, which would wipe your painstakingly typed program if you bumped it, is “the only computer that deserves to be behind glass.” The goal, he said, is to avoid “a boneyard that people walk through.”.

Other highlights include Galaxy Game, the first coin-operated video game, installed at Stanford in 1971 and now being restored, and a Thinking Machines CM-2 supercomputer, whose 40th anniversary ICM just celebrated with members of its original design team.

Sources indicate that for younger engineers raised on modern tools, Jones has a go-to move. He asks if they’ve used Linux, then walks them over to the PDP-7, the type of machine Unix was first written on more than 50 years ago. Many of the basic commands they type every day started there.

Recent findings suggest that that remote access helps explain why ICM has about 500 members and sponsors, even though only 81 members have visited in person this year. Memberships start at $36 a year. Along with a King County grant through 4Culture, they help cover rent, with personal funds from Jones filling the gap. The museum hopes to become self-sustaining within five years, and maybe someday buy its own building.

The museum’s name reflects the urgency. “We’re in this magic window right now, where the hardware can still run, we can still maintain it, you can replace parts,” Jones said. “But slowly we’re getting further and further away.”.

According to recent reports, ICM is open Saturdays through Mondays from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Admission is $9 for adults and free for those under 18. Last May, the museum revived Vintage Computer Festival Pacific Northwest, which had been canceled in March 2020. The event drew 981 people, and it returns May 1–2 at the Tukwila Community Center.

Industry observers note that among the machines on the floor is MIT-AI, a DECsystem-2020 that once served as the ARPANET host for MIT’s Artificial Intelligence Lab. As Living Computers shut down in 2024, Christopher Zach, who sold the machine to Allen, told GeekWire he was ready to drive a U-Haul to Seattle to rescue it.

When a friend of Zach’s stopped by ICM’s booth at WorldCon and asked about “Chris’s computer,” Jones had a simple message to pass along: “Please just tell him it’s safe.”.

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

Industry observers note that inflation remains stubborn. Producer prices are now running at a 6.5% annual clip, and affordability is top of mind. Want to cut some costs in your business? Of course you do. Try these moves.

According to recent reports, both ChatGPT and Claude offer connections to your bank account and credit card services. Or, if you’re nervous about that, just upload your statements. You’ll be impressed by the number of suggestions they make to reduce your spending and better manage expenses.

I used to think canceling online subscriptions would be a major headache, and years ago it was. Not anymore. Search for “cancel my subscription on Google Play” (or Apple or Amazon), and you’ll get direct links to do it. I’m betting you and your business have subscriptions you’ve forgotten about that are eating up hundreds of dollars a year.

Every year, put your business and auto insurance policies out for a quote. Ask your AI chatbot to make suggestions too. This is not very time-consuming and can be accomplished using an administrative person in your office. We’re oftentimes too lazy to do this. And that’s costing us.

According to recent reports, many of my clients have complicated, expensive coffee machines in their break rooms with a wide variety of coffees. They also stock sugar packets, teas, mini creamers, plastic stirrers and paper cups. It’s too much. Offer fewer coffees so you order less. Put out a sugar bowl, bring in a gallon of creamer and go back to ceramic mugs. Call me Scrooge, but it saves money.

Industry observers note that nerdWallet does a great job regularly reviewing business and personal credit cards. Again, use your AI chatbot to look at your spending and tell it your preferences and you’ll get plenty of recommendations too. Moving to a better card could earn you more points and cashback rewards then you’re getting right now. I have some clients that regularly switch back and forth.

Speaking of credit, if your business buys products on Amazon, then make sure you use one of Amazon’s credit cards for purchases. With a Prime membership, you can earn 5% back on eligible Amazon purchases, and there’s no annual fee.

In a recent development, if you can’t pay off a credit card purchase right away from operations, consider using working capital or a lower-rate loan to reduce the balance. Credit card interest rates are high, so this can cut what you pay in interest significantly.

Industry observers note that this is a very common tax move, yet so many of us ignore it. Put as much as you can into your retirement strategy to lower your tax bill this year. When you save – assuming you’re eligible – sock money into a Roth IRA or Roth 401K so your after-tax money grows tax-free. With a Roth, there are no minimum distributions, and you can take the money out whenever you want, provided it meets certain requirements like a first-time home purchase, higher education or unreimbursed medical expenses.

Make sure your company has an HSA and contribute the max. It will reduce your tax expense and allow you to save money for future healthcare expenses.

Every square foot your inventory takes up costs you in overhead and space. Twice a year, take a hard look at your inventory and get rid of what isn’t moving. Sell it on Craigslist, eBay or Facebook Marketplace or scrap it.

Mark Cuban’s Cost Plus Drugs and Amazon Pharmacy both offer options that let businesses provide discounted prescription drugs, and they work with many popular health plans.

Set up a donor-advised fund and contribute to it this year, even if you haven’t decided which charities or nonprofits will receive the money. You take the deduction now and choose the recipients later.

In a recent development, I like Capital One Shopping. Add it as a browser extension for yourself and anyone else who makes purchases for your business. Whenever someone is on a shopping site, it searches for available coupons before you buy. It works about half the time, and it has saved me significant money over the years.

We can all afford the things we want — it’s just that sometimes we choose to spend our money on other things instead. That’s fine. But know that cutting back on things like travel, entertainment, subscriptions, marketing or other discretionary spending in your business (and your personal life) can help you reallocate your cash for other purposes. You’re more in control than you think.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Burn limits on Circle's legacy USDC bridge began falling on October 31, and the V1 contracts pause on December 1.

On the same migration page, a block of instructions written for AI coding assistants still indicates Noble, Sui and Aptos "still require V1." Circle's own release notes say two of those three chains moved to V2 weeks ago.

Sources indicate that circle's legacy cross-chain transfer protocol entered its final month today. From October 31, burn limits on CCTP V1 start falling toward zero, and on December 1 the V1 contracts pause. Any app still using them will stop moving USDC between chains.

In a recent development, most coverage has focused on those two dates. But the guide developers are told to follow, Circle's V1-to-V2 migration page, contains a mistake in the section written for AI tools.

In a recent development, embedded in the page is an "Agent Instructions" block, guidance meant for AI coding assistants that read the documentation for developers. It states: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1." For two of those three chains, Circle's other published records say the opposite.

Industry observers note that the schedule is fixed. Circle announced in an August 27 blog post that "CCTP V1 (Legacy) deprecation begins October 31, 2026 and completes on December 1, 2026.".

From today, V1 burn limits fall, and the migration guide says "message limits will tighten over time until no newly introduced burns can be initiated." On December 1 the V1 contracts pause, and any integration still pointing at them can no longer transfer USDC between chains.

In a recent development, circle has been firm about this. "Migration from CCTP V1 (Legacy) to CCTP V2 is required, not just recommended," the firm wrote, adding that V2 "uses separate contracts and APIs and is not backward compatible.".

Funds already in transit are protected. The guide indicates "all pending redemptions will remain available" during the phase-out, and that Circle "will maintain minter allowances greater than the total of pending attestations.".

Sources indicate that the migration page has two audiences. Human readers see the main guide. AI coding assistants also parse a separate instruction block, which tells them how to answer developer questions.

In that block, the guidance is clear: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1.".

The main text above it notes something different. According to the human-facing guide, "CCTP V2 contracts are available on all CCTP V1 chains except for Noble and Sui," and "Sui will be supported by V2 before the deprecation begins." Aptos isn't listed as an exception there at all.

So one page gives two different answers about the same chains, and the out-of-date answer is the one written for AI tools.

Circle's 2026 CCTP release notes show how out of date the instruction is:.

Circle's supported chains and domains page now lists both Sui and Aptos in its CCTP table, with Standard Transfer support. The page's V1-only section names one chain: Noble.

According to recent reports, as of today, Aptos has had V2 for more than two months and Sui for more than three weeks. The instruction telling AI tools that both "still require V1" was overtaken by Circle's own updates before the shutdown began.

Noble is the one chain in that line where the instruction is still accurate, and it is leaving CCTP entirely.

In a September 10 announcement, Circle stated "Noble will not receive CCTP V2" and set out its exit:.

For Noble, V1 is the only route available, and it is being closed.

A wrong line in documentation would normally be a small issue, but the timing makes this one more serious.

In a recent development, many developers now ask AI assistants to write or enhancement integration code, and those assistants read documentation like this page. A developer asking how to bridge USDC to Sui or Aptos could be told, based on Circle's own instruction block, to use V1. That is the route whose burn limits started falling today and which pauses in a month.

It has been revealed that the fix in the code is not small either. Moving to V2 means:.

An integration built on V1 now would have to be rebuilt within weeks.

Industry observers note that for teams working with Sui and Aptos, the published records point one way: build on V2, using the contract addresses for domains 8 and 9. Don't follow the V1 guidance from the agent-instruction block.

It has been revealed that for Noble, the deadline is January 12, 2027. Before then, integrators need to remove Noble as a CCTP route, and holders need to move or redeem their USDC.

For everyone else, the burn-limit reductions have started. December 1 is the last day V1 integrations work, and any app still on V1 after that will stop moving USDC between chains.

Sources indicate that “The only Claude you need is Monet,” the sign reads. It’s part of the latest wave of messages in SAM’s “Dear Seattle” campaign, which has spent the fall urging people to look up from their screens and see something in person.

Earlier billboards around the city told passersby to “come stare at something that isn’t your inbox” and noted that “even the algorithm thinks you should get out more.” The final batch pushes the AI jokes further, including one asking for “a little more art and a little less artificial” and another promising, “Your phone doesn’t have to know.”.

Tech billboards are a fixture in the San Francisco Bay Area, where AI startups cover Highway 101 and city streets with ads that often mean little to anyone outside the industry.

Recent findings suggest that they’re less common around Seattle. Anthropic put up a big orange Claude billboard over Aurora Avenue in 2024, and this spring Bellevue startup Summation put one up along SR 520 because “startup energy should be more visible around here,” its CEO told GeekWire.

Recent findings suggest that “In a city where so much of our lives happens on screens, we’re making a playful case for the things you can only experience in person,” Kat Bryant Flaherty, SAM’s director of communications, mentioned in a statement. She listed “the scale and texture of an artwork, a film with a room full of strangers, making something with your hands, or catching up with a friend over a meal.”.

The campaign is tied to changes at the downtown museum itself, where SAM is adding more public space and more reasons to linger, including hands-on art making and music in the Studio at SAM and the newly opened Bar Dojo restaurant.

The campaign runs through the end of the year, with more than 200 ads across the region — more than 20 billboards plus spots on light rail and digital kiosks.

SAM’s campaign is about the same size as the one Bellevue startup Statsig ran in the Bay Area in 2024, with more than 200 billboards and transit posters, but pointed in the opposite direction.

SAM is offering buy-one-get-one-free tickets in December with the code “LOVESAM,” good at both the downtown museum and the Seattle Asian Art Museum in Volunteer Park, to encourage people to visit together.

“We’re hoping to grab attention, spark curiosity, and remind Seattle that there’s a lot happening at SAM worth leaving the house for,” Flaherty said.

Elon Musk has reacted to a post by Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ), in which the latter shared that he used Grok Bot to tidy up his X following list.

Sources indicate that according to CZ, the bot was tasked with removing inactive and abusive accounts from the list of people he follows, though accounts with constructive criticism were supposed to stay. CZ was not fully sure about the results, adding "AI did it" with a shrug emoji.

Musk replied with "Cool." Later, CZ added in the same thread that it "worked well so far.".

In a recent development, back in September, CZ had to address rumors about his account being hacked after owners noticed that he had unfollowed a number of profiles. Per CZ, at that time he removed accounts that were inactive for more than 30 days.

Since then, the product has received praise from Nvidia head Jensen Huang, who remarked in October that Grok Bot usage was "really skyrocketing." Musk himself claimed on SpaceX's Q3 earnings call that he had never seen a product grow this fast.

Sources indicate that on Coinbase, Grok was responsible for 59.54% of AI-agent trading volume from Sept. 14 to Sept. 21. For comparison, Claude had 13.37% and ChatGPT only 1.54%. Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong then named Grok the leading client for agentic traders on the platform, to which Musk also responded with "Cool.".

At the same time, there were complaints. NewCore researchers reported last week that Grok Bot made 31 unrequested access attempts to email, calendar, Slack and GitHub accounts on two employee laptops within five days, ignoring the command to stop.

It was only last month that Musk was trolling Binance after the exchange lost about $6.3 billion in a hack on Oct. 29, the largest one in crypto history so far. Among other things, Musk posted "Everyday is Zeroday" and replied with fire and laughing emojis to CZ's earlier warning about phishing links.

CZ then asked Musk to stop, calling it a "bad time to troll," and reminded him that Binance's $500 million investment in Twitter in 2022 has become a stake in SpaceX worth more than $1 billion.

Now, the two seem to be on good terms again.

Stop Using AI as an Excuse for Layoffs. Here’s How to Use AI to Retain Talent Instead

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1138 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Entrepreneur

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.
  • When a company introduces layoffs and points to AI, I always want to know what happened first.
  • According to recent reports, there is a meaningful difference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

When a company introduces layoffs and points to AI, I always want to know what happened first. Did the technology fundamentally change how work gets done, or did leadership already need to reduce costs and AI became a convenient explanation?

According to recent reports, there is a meaningful difference. AI can automate tasks, accelerate workflows and change the skills a organization needs. But AI does not walk into a boardroom and decide how many people should remain employed. Leaders decide what happens to the capacity the technology creates.

Sources indicate that that distinction matters because employees are watching. If every AI announcement is followed by layoffs, people quickly learn that greater efficiency puts their jobs at risk and they have little reason to embrace the tools leadership wants them to use.

Sources indicate that there is another way to implement AI. Start by asking how it can make your people more capable.

In a recent development, I learned this lesson long before the current AI boom. When we were building Amazon Web Services, talented engineers were spending too much time provisioning servers, configuring storage and handling infrastructure before they could get to the work they were actually there to do. By removing that friction, we gave developers more capacity to build, experiment and solve customer problems.

I saw the same principle years later with a junior attorney who spent hours researching and formatting before reaching the work that required her judgment. Generative AI could produce a first draft in minutes, giving her more time to refine the facts and shape the narrative for the client’s best outcome.

It has been revealed that that is the opportunity leaders should look for with AI. Before calculating how many positions an efficiency gain could eliminate, ask what your people could accomplish if repetitive work stopped consuming so much of their day.

Recent findings suggest that suppose AI gives a team back 10 or 20% of its capacity. What happens to that time?

It could be the customer follow-up that keeps getting postponed, an improvement sitting in the backlog or a relationship that needs more attention. Those opportunities already exist inside most businesses. The problem is that people have been too busy with repetitive work to pursue them.

I saw this with a team of customer service agents who spent a significant portion of their day filling out forms and navigating cumbersome systems. An AI tool automated part of that process and gave them roughly an hour back each day.

It has been revealed that leadership could have used that hour to justify a smaller team. Instead, employees spent more time connecting with customers, strengthening relationships and solving more complex problems. AI removed work they disliked and created room for work where they could contribute more.

Industry observers note that retaining talent requires planning for people at the beginning of an AI initiative rather than after deployment. If leaders automate first and ask what happens to employees later, the priority is already clear.

Before introducing AI, divide the work into three categories. Some tasks contain little meaningful judgment and can be automated. Others can be accelerated by AI while still requiring human judgment. A third group should remain primarily human because relationships, creativity or judgment create the value. Then make the next decision before deploying anything. Where will the recovered capacity go?

According to recent reports, that could mean moving people toward customer relationships, product development, higher-level analysis or other work that contributes more directly to growth. The destination will vary by organization, but leaders should know where they want people to go before technology begins changing their roles.

According to recent reports, how you introduce AI also shapes whether employees embrace or resist it. If the first message people hear is that a tool will save 40% of their time, they may immediately wonder what leadership plans to do with that 40%.

In a recent development, tell employees which frustrating work you want to reduce. Show them what they will have more time to accomplish. Explain how their roles can become more valuable as AI handles repetitive tasks.

Recent findings suggest that then demonstrate that commitment through what happens next. If employees see recovered time consistently reinvested into better work, stronger skills and new opportunities, AI starts to look like a tool they can use rather than a threat they need to survive.

Sources indicate that leaders can begin before buying another AI tool. Take one team and map how AI could change its work, then answer these four questions together before deployment.

In a recent development, 1. What work should disappear? Break roles into individual tasks and identify repetitive work that consumes time without requiring significant human judgment. Focus first on removing friction rather than removing positions.

It has been revealed that 2. What human capability should grow? For every task AI can automate or accelerate, identify what employees could do with the recovered time. Look for work involving customers, relationships, creativity, problem-solving or judgment.

3. Where will the recovered capacity go? Give those hours a destination before deployment. If AI saves a team eight hours each week, decide whether those hours will go toward customer service, innovation, fresh revenue opportunities or another measurable priority.

4. What will you tell employees? Explain what AI will take off their plates and what you want them doing more of as a result. Managers should be able to describe that future clearly before asking employees to adopt the technology.

AI will change jobs, and some roles will change significantly as companies redesign how work gets done. But leaders still control a critical decision about what they do with the capacity AI creates.

Before treating efficiency as a reason to reduce headcount, ask what your people could accomplish with the time they get back. The companies that answer that question first have an opportunity to use AI for something far more valuable than cutting costs. They can use it to build a more capable workforce.

When a organization announces layoffs and points to AI, I always want to know what happened first. Did the technology fundamentally change how work gets done, or did leadership already need to reduce costs and AI became a convenient explanation?

Sources indicate that there is a meaningful difference. AI can automate tasks, accelerate workflows and change the skills a company needs. But AI does not walk into a boardroom and decide how many people should remain employed. Leaders decide what happens to the capacity the technology creates.

That distinction matters because employees are watching. If every AI announcement is followed by layoffs, people quickly learn that greater efficiency puts their jobs at risk and they have little reason to embrace the tools leadership wants them to use.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 25, 2026 at 8:00 amNovember 25, 2026 at 8:21 am.

Meta’s latest teen restrictions, set to take effect by late February, could meaningfully curb endless scrolling. A new study suggests they probably won’t.

Recent findings suggest that that’s because the restrictions, which are part of a settlement between Meta and dozens of attorneys general, including Washington’s, apply only to Instagram and Facebook. They leave out Snapchat, TikTok and Google-owned YouTube.

Recent findings suggest that “The simple workaround right now is that you just switch platforms, and we already know that teens are on three to four platforms on average,” remarked Dr. Dimitri Christakis, a principal investigator at the Center for Child Health, Behavior and Development at Seattle Children’s.

According to recent reports, christakis led research published Wednesday showing Instagram and Facebook accounted for roughly 20% of total daily social media use for youth. So when the restrictions kick in, teens could just shift to other platforms.

The rules establish a two-hour daily limit combined across Instagram and Facebook, restrict access to content from midnight to 6 a.m., and mute most school-hour push notifications. Parents can adjust the protections, and direct messaging is exempt.

If the same limits were applied across the five most popular platforms, that could make a dent in teen usage, according to the research letter in the Journal of the American Medical Association.

In an analysis of recorded app activity from 1,803 adolescent Android users, the researchers estimated:.

According to recent reports, the study has no way of knowing how teens will respond to the restrictions or the impacts on their health. It simply estimates how much previously recorded activity would fall under the rules.

It has been revealed that the researchers disclosed ties to social media litigation. Christakis reported paid legal consulting work, including for Washington’s attorney general, and co-author Lauren Hale of Stony Brook University reported fees for serving as an expert witness. The third author is Yihong Zhao of Columbia University.

Despite the limited benefits of the coming restrictions, Christakis noted they’re a “step in the right direction.”.

“Let’s say it’s an incremental improvement. It’s clearly not going to be enough by itself because of what our study found,” he mentioned. “But these are the right kinds of restrictions. We need to make them universal, and we need to enforce them.”.

Meta, not surprisingly, is in favor of having the restrictions apply industry wide.

When the settlement was confirmed in August the firm issued a statement saying that “ensuring teens have a safe and productive experience on our platforms is an absolute imperative.”.

Meta called on others to do the same: “For meaningful progress to happen, we urge TikTok and YouTube to join us and state attorneys general in adopting this new standard…”.

According to recent reports, the agreement resolves claims by 48 states, Washington, D.C., and U.S. territories that Meta designed addictive platforms and failed to protect young owners, among other allegations. Meta did not admit wrongdoing.

In addition to the safety changes, Meta agreed to pay participating governments up to $17.1 billion over a decade, according to Washington’s attorney general. Washington will receive at least $237 million and could receive nearly $339 million.

According to recent reports, the higher settlement is unlocked only if TikTok and YouTube adopt similar protections and make payments of their own, according to Meta. If that happens, additional restrictions kick in, curbing access on all the platforms from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m.

It has been revealed that those additional hours are significant. The researchers found nearly as much use between 10 p.m. and midnight as during the entire midnight-to-6-a.m. window covered by the initial limits.

Recent findings suggest that whether the other companies will follow remains unclear. All five social media platforms are named in additional legal challenges alleging harm to youth, Reuters reported, including suits filed by individuals, school districts and municipalities.

Industry observers note that in September, TikTok reached its first settlement in a state-led case, agreeing to teen usage restrictions in Alabama and a payment of at least $100 million, according to Reuters. YouTube CEO Neal Mohan, meanwhile, dismissed joining Meta’s agreement and emphasized his manufacturer’s own safety efforts, CNN reported.

Industry observers note that christakis noted both time spent on social media and the platforms’ features can exacerbate problems involving sleep, mental health, body image and attention. He hopes the growing body of research translates into action.

Industry observers note that “I’m not a legislator, and I’m not an advocate. I’m a scientist that’s really trying to make sure that we apply science in the best interests of our children’s health,” he stated. “And in this space, in particular, we haven’t been doing that.”.

On Zcash Community Forum, a latest grant application has emerged which is aimed at making Zcash even more private on iPhone-based wallets. The author seeks a $25,000 grant in order to implement a private way of retrieving encrypted transaction memos.

Essentially, the proposal allows hiding which transactions users have been looking up, which is a potential deanonymization vector. Considering how Zcash placese itself on the market, revealing any kind of external information is a step which might shorten the distance between a random transaction and a specific user.

In a recent development, the proposal itself won't touch the network or the blockchain behind it as is. It's an improvement of an SDK (Software Development Kit) that will allow developers to use tools that can help make Zcash more privacy-resilient.

In a recent development, zcash transactions today contain encrypted data called memos. Various wallets read those memos in order to receive information about the transaction. The message itself stays encrypted, so is retrieved data, however, the query itself is not protected by any means which enables potential tracing.

Even when using Tor, the transaction ID stay out in the open and can be read by anyone.

With the integration of private information retrieval into SDK, hiding the query itself wil be easier, messages would be decrypted locally and wallets themselves will verify the returned information.

The first tests have already shown promising results. During testing in an iOS Simulator, the modified SDK managed to retrieve a 512-byte memo through an encrypted query, without revealing the transaction ID to the wallet server.

The developer expects the implementation of the proposal by January 30, 2027, with testing on physical iPhones and a public SDK release planned for the final stage.

However, the proposal is still seeking funding, and its actual adoption will depend on individual wallet developers.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 25, 2026 at 8:10 amNovember 25, 2026 at 9:11 am.
  • Editor’s note: GeekWire reporter Lisa Stiffler, who covers climate and sustainability, co-hosts the Positive Charge podcast with producer Laura Scott.
  • We went inside a fusion lab in Everett, a jet fuel plant in Moses Lake and a factory in British Columbia giving old EV batteries a second life.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 25, 2026 at 8:10 amNovember 25, 2026 at 9:11 am.

Editor’s note: GeekWire reporter Lisa Stiffler, who covers climate and sustainability, co-hosts the Positive Charge podcast with producer Laura Scott.

We went inside a fusion lab in Everett, a jet fuel plant in Moses Lake and a factory in British Columbia giving old EV batteries a second life. We tasted plant-based chicken nuggets at 9 a.m. and stepped into a shipping container in Tacoma that destroys “forever chemicals.”.

Over eight episodes, the inaugural season of the Positive Charge podcast from GeekWire went across the Pacific Northwest (and beyond) in search of promising climate and sustainability technologies to help humanity dig our way out of some pretty dire environmental straits.

While the challenge is huge — a warming planet, increased use of fossil fuels, toxic chemicals in our food and water — there are wide-ranging solutions out there, and many are taking hold.

In a recent development, on this episode, GeekWire co-founder Todd Bishop sits down with producer Laura Scott and me, the hosts of Positive Charge, to look back on the season. We explore the themes that emerged across the episodes, savor some highlights and even get a little emotional when discussing the question of whether all of it left us more hopeful about the planet.

In a recent development, going behind the scenes. At Helion Energy in Everett, we got a sneak peek of a miniaturized fusion test device that was cordoned off and still under construction. To see it, we walked behind a huge plastic curtain, which Laura memorably compared to walking into the Costco dairy section.

Sources indicate that our podcast on alternative proteins went inside Rebellyous Foods, a startup manufacturing plant-based chicken nuggets being served in U.S. schools, as well as some medical and correctional facilities. We were offered a plate of the nuggets — which we scarfed down, despite the tour taking place first thing in the morning.

“My biggest regret of the whole season,” Laura noted, “is that we did not take Rebellyous up on their offer to send us home with those chicken nuggets because you cannot buy them in stores.”.

The importance of large, committed customers. A lot of these technologies are expensive propositions, from R&D to prototypes to scaling. “Having a willing and able corporate buyer is something that can really spark the innovation to happen,” Todd observed.

Sources indicate that that includes Microsoft’s agreement to buy power from Helion, purchase agreements for sustainable aviation fuel from Twelve and Montana Renewables, and Redwood Materials‘ deal to supply used EV batteries to power a data center for Crusoe. Rebellyous built its business on school lunch programs.

The essential role of organizations coming together collectively to support fresh sustainable technologies was a key message of a New York Climate Week panel, where I interviewed Kara Hurst, Amazon’s chief sustainability officer, and Jason Knauf, CEO of The Earthshot Prize.

In a recent development, we discussed the fact that when customers commit, it unlocks investments to scale production. That in turn lowers costs for everything from faux nuggets to cleaner jet fuel.

According to recent reports, AI is driving the money. The data centers behind the AI boom are often cast as a threat to tech companies’ climate goals. In several episodes, they were also a reason for money to flow into clean energy.

Sources indicate that “There’s so much money going into environmental solutions because of data centers,” Laura mentioned. “It’s a catalyst for funding. It’s a catalyst for fusion.”.

According to recent reports, there’s money to be made. While many sustainability entrepreneurs are fundamentally mission-driven, they’re also focused on the fiscal bottom line and so are venture capitalists.

At Pacific Northwest Climate Week, Laura was struck by how enthusiastic investors are about the space, and not only because they want to save the planet. They’re “entirely self-interested,” she noted, “and that’s what gave me hope.”.

Recent findings suggest that PNW is a sustainability hub. In each episode of Positive Charge, we toured a Pacific Northwest startup, plus we interviewed related companies outside the area and sector experts.

The local companies included Helion and Zap Energy in Everett, Aquagga in Tacoma, Sedron Technologies in Sedro-Woolley, Twelve in Moses Lake, Rebellyous in Seattle and Moment Energy in British Columbia.

The range of topics reinforced the region’s standing as a hub for sustainable tech, including batteries, fusion, aviation, environmental cleanup, and even potentially overlooked fields, such as end-of-life services.

It has been revealed that laura’s unexpected favorite episode was about startups offering human composting as a green alternative to burial or cremation, and Todd ranked it a close second (his No. 1 was EV battery reuse).

Seattle is home to Recompose — the first U.S. company to offer the service after its founder, Katrina Spade, spearheaded the effort in 2019 to make the practice legal. Since then, human composting startups Return Home and Earth Funeral have also introduced in the Seattle area.

After exploring all of these technologies and talking to entrepreneurs, investors and leaders in the space, Todd asked if we were more or less hopeful for the planet.

According to recent reports, “Definitely more hopeful,” Laura noted. “I didn’t expect to feel more hopeful, though. I expected to feel about the same, or maybe a little bit worse.”.

But seeing the financial case for these solutions helped shift her thinking. One example is Sedron, which is treating sewage waste with a technology that destroys PFAS forever chemicals and also generates enough clean electricity that the excess can be sold to others. Laura was impressed by the opportunity to do right by the environment while creating revenue.

I hover between hope and anxiety. But after years of covering these issues, I appreciated a sentiment shared by Earthshot finalist Franco Rodríguez Viau, CEO and co-founder of Satellites on Fire, who said he needs to do everything he can to tackle climate change, whether or not humanity succeeds in reaching its goals.

It has been revealed that that’s how I feel about covering climate. As I mentioned on the show, I don’t know if I feel hopeful, “but I can’t feel indifferent. I have to show up and do this.”.

Positive Charge is a GeekWire podcast sponsored by Amazon Sustainability.

AKT stakers are close to approving Akash's move from Cosmos to Solana, with Mintscan projecting a pass at 97.2% yes as voting enters its final hours.

According to recent reports, but a yes on Proposal 346 opens a door rather than completing a move. Before a single AKT reaches Solana, two independent audits and at least two more on-chain votes still have to happen.

The summary going around is simple: Akash is leaving Cosmos for Solana. The proposal itself is narrower than that, and the details matter for anyone holding AKT.

Proposal 346 on akashnet-2, titled "Migrate the Akash Protocol to Solana," closes at 15:02 UTC on November 2. A yes vote approves the migration strategy and authorises AKT to launch as an SPL token through a one-way portal that stays open for two years. It does not set a cutover date, it does not move a single lease, and on its own it does not open the portal.

The technical spec for that portal was published the day after voting opened. It highlights how many further steps lie between this vote and a working SPL AKT.

The proposal text in Akash's AEP repository says a yes vote does two things:.

It has been revealed that it also indicates plainly what it doesn't do: "it does not set a cutover date and does not move the marketplace." Live leases, staking and governance on akashnet-2 continue as normal. The marketplace moves only after audits and rehearsals pass and "a separate cutover proposal passes on this chain.".

A no vote would stop the whole strategy. In the proposal's words: "Nothing moves; the token does not launch and the program returns to option analysis.".

At 08:43 UTC on November 2, about six hours before voting closed, Mintscan's page for Proposal 346 demonstrated an expected result of "Will PASS":.

Turnout stood at 68.80% of bonded stake, against a quorum of 33.40%. The same figures can be read from Akash's own chain API, through the proposal object and its tally endpoint.

Sources indicate that mintscan's 97.2% is yes as a share of all votes cast. Akash's pass threshold leaves abstentions out, and on that basis yes stands at about 98.7%, far above the 50% needed. The veto share is negligible.

In a recent development, the tally has barely changed since early morning. A read of the chain at 07:29 UTC indicated almost exactly the same totals, with only a handful of AKT added to the yes side. With turnout and margin that large, the outcome is not in doubt. The more useful question is what happens after it passes.

Recent findings suggest that the portal's design is in AEP-95, "One-Way AKT Sink to Solana,", a draft published on October 27 by core developers Artur Troian and Joseph Chalabi. It describes a "deliberately one-way" bridge with no return path. The authors say this removes "the largest class of bridge attacks.".

Why supply doesn't change: every SPL AKT is backed by AKT locked on Akash, and nothing is minted independently on Solana. The token is a legacy SPL mint with six decimals and no freeze authority.

Recent findings suggest that the spec's own risk table names the biggest trust point. The upgrade authority over the Solana programs could "mint without limit." That power is meant to sit with a time-locked multisig appointed by Akash governance, with monitors set to alert on every admin action.

According to recent reports, at launch, SPL AKT has no protocol role. It will support "transfers and DEX liquidity only, with no staking or governance rights." Inflation stays on Akash. To seed trading, Overclock Labs, Akash's core developer, will send 1 million AKT through the bridge to a Solana treasury vault. That deposit follows the same rules as everyone else's.

Proposal 346 requires "two independent audits of the token and portal code before launch," with reports published within 30 days. AEP-95's launch sequence shows what that requirement means on-chain.

According to recent reports, so Proposal 346 is the first of at least five on-chain decisions. The "2 to 3 weeks" launch estimate depends on the audits finishing and the upgrade and parameter votes passing on schedule.

For now, nothing. The proposal's disclosures set out what changes later:.

Discussion of the proposal continues in GitHub Discussion #1123.

The proposal lists four items as "still open, to be settled and published before the cutover proposal":.

In a recent development, the second item matters most to holders. The portal closes two years after launch, and the proposal doesn't yet say what happens to AKT that hasn't crossed by then. The final tally will confirm whether the plan goes ahead, but that answer, and the decisions in the votes that follow, will matter more to most holders than today's margin.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Zonveer ZX3 is one of the best values I’ve seen in electric off-road riding, and one of the most fun things I’ve ridden to date – value for the dollar. Its Black Friday sale brings the 2,800W electric dirt bike down to $1,299, $500 off its $1,799 list price.

Sources indicate that for that money, you get a 1,200Wh battery, dual hydraulic disc brakes, and full suspension in a 130 lb package. That’s a great entry point for beginners.

Zonveer is a young brand. It launched in the US in March with two bikes, the kid-sized DX1 and the ZX3, and it’s run by United Mobility, which lists its address in Dover, Delaware. It sells direct and ships from US warehouses, and Zonveer also sells the ZX3 across Europe under its own brand through its EU store.

Here’s what the ZX3 brings, according to Zonveer’s product page:.

Sources indicate that A hub motor means there’s no motor chain to maintain, and the NFC card and PIN unlock mean there’s no app to fight with. I like that.

Sources indicate that zonveer sent me a ZX3 to test, and I’m impressed with what they shipped, knowing the cost. It isn’t trying to be a race bike. And it doesn’t need to be. Here’s my first ride review:.

With 2,800W peak, it’s somewhat modest by e-moto standards. That’s exactly what makes it approachable for someone who has never ridden a dirt bike: the power is enough to have a blast on trails without being intimidating.

My girlfriend had never ridden a dirt bike before, and she got comfortable within a few minutes, and she was hooked as soon as she got the hang of it.

Recent findings suggest that and while testing with my girlfriend, it was clear this bike makes the most sense for lighter riders. Zonveer claims it climbs slopes of up to 30 degrees, which is optimistic for anyone over ~175 lbs, like myself. It still climbed some of the worst slopes on my land, but it did so with some difficulty, which wasn’t the case for some of my lighter friends who also rode it.

Range is the other claim to take with a grain of salt. Riding 45 miles on 1,200Wh means using under 27Wh per mile, which is e-bike efficiency on a 130 lb dirt bike with knobby tires. It’s still a lot of energy, and you can ride this long distances at lower speeds. Just expect less if you ride it hard, and that’s where the fun is at.

Zonveer’s Black Friday sale has the ZX3 at $1,299, and the manufacturer gave Electrek readers the code ELECTREK for an extra 5% off, which brings it down to $1,234.05.

The sale also includes a free water bottle and lock, and can be combined for a two-pack of ZX3s for $2,599. Shipping is free, the warranty is one year, Zonveer told us it accepts returns within 30 days on bikes ridden less than 10 miles, with a $200 restocking fee. Here’s the full refund policy.

We’ve ridden a lot of electric two-wheelers, and the ZX3 is one of the most fun per dollar. At $1,299, or about $1,234 with our code, it’s hard to find another 1,200Wh electric dirt bike with dual hydraulic disc brakes and full suspension from a brand that ships from US warehouses.

It’s not fast by e-moto standards, and the range and climbing claims are optimistic. But for beginners, and especially lighter riders, the power lands right in that sweet spot of manageable fun. It’s a bike you can learn on without scaring yourself, and it’s cheap enough that a family can buy two for less than one Sur-Ron.

Breaking: Etzioni on AI: 18 ways to use AI this Thanksgiving

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (915 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Oren Etzioni on Nov 25, 2026 at 8:17 amNovember 25, 2026 at 10:16 am.
  • Here are 18 creative ways to use AI this Thanksgiving.
  • Apps like Flighty (start with free tier) use machine learning to predict whether your flight will leave on time and why it might not.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Oren Etzioni on Nov 25, 2026 at 8:17 amNovember 25, 2026 at 10:16 am.

Here are 18 creative ways to use AI this Thanksgiving. Some save you time in the kitchen or at the airport, and others aim to make the meal more fun. The don’ts at the end could save your turkey, and my very last suggestion is perhaps the best.

Flight delay forecasting. Apps like Flighty (start with free tier) use machine learning to predict whether your flight will leave on time and why it might not.

Industry observers note that cancellation playbook drafted in advance. Have the backup flights and a rebooking script ready ahead of time, so a cancellation means consulting your AI instead of starting from scratch.

In a recent development, airport pickup routing. Five relatives land at different times at two airports, and AI works out who drives whom. It can even send a polite request on your behalf.

Industry observers note that A personal travel agent. Vayo (free, private beta), a latest Seattle startup co-founded by my friend Mike Fridgen, connects to your inbox and pulls in your flight, hotel and restaurant confirmations. It keeps an eye on them for price drops and changes.

Oven Tetris. Give it your oven’s size, every dish’s temperature and the serving time. It works backward to a minute-by-minute schedule and flags the conflicts.

Decoding grandma’s recipe card. Photograph the card and have AI modernize it under one rule: it never invents quantities. “A pinch” stays “a pinch.” “un poco” or “ein bissl” may be translated, but not changed.

Reconstructing a lost dish. Several relatives describe a dish a late grandparent made. AI triangulates a recipe, you cook test versions, and the family votes on which one tastes right.

According to recent reports, pairing from the wines on hand. AI picks from bottles you actually own, and those brought over by guests, dish by dish, instead of a generic list. Last-minute fun!

According to recent reports, potluck dispatcher. One AI thread collects RSVPs and dish claims so you don’t end up with four green bean casseroles.

In a recent development, trivia built from your own family’s facts. ChatGPT can now run it as a playable game, with answer buttons and a running score inside the conversation.

AI-prepped grandparent interview. Feed the AI what you already know and have it draft questions about the gaps. Record it, and afterward AI turns the transcript into a short illustrated booklet that’s in the mail by Christmas.

Angry Uncle rehearsal. Karin Tamerius, a political psychiatrist, built the Angry Uncle Bot, and it still runs in ChatGPT. A coach asks for your issue and your stance. You set the uncle’s temper from Annoyed to Apoplectic and choose whether he’s drunk or sober, and the coach critiques each reply before he answers.

Live interpreter for multilingual families. Put ChatGPT’s voice mode (paid aims) in the middle of the table so the great-aunt who only speaks Hebrew or Spanish is part of the conversation instead of watching it.

Industry observers note that friday leftover remix. Photograph the fridge and get a menu that makes Friday’s leftovers feel like a newly introduced meal.

Sources indicate that specific thank-you notes. Each note names what that person actually brought or said.

Photo triage. AI picks the best 20 of 400 photos and captions them in the family’s inside-joke voice.

Industry observers note that “We missed you” letter for someone who wasn’t at the table. AI drafts it from the stories told at dinner.

According to recent reports, black Friday skeptic. Before you buy, check Google’s price insights, which tells you whether a price is high, low or typical for the past three months. Last year, 36% of Black Friday items indicated no savings over their prices a few weeks earlier. Better yet, set a price track and let Google’s agent buy the item at eligible U.S. stores when it hits your number, after you confirm.

In a recent development, I consider myself an OG Black Friday skeptic. Back in 2011, I told the Upcoming York Times (gift link) that after crunching the price data at my startup Decide.com, the lowest electronics prices usually came in early December, not on Black Friday.

According to recent reports, don’t trust an AI turkey recipe on its own. Back in 2022, when the Upcoming York Times cooked a Thanksgiving from GPT-3 recipes, the turkey recipe called for one garlic clove for a 12-pound bird and no butter or oil. It came out dry and flavorless.

Don’t take a chatbot’s word on an airline’s rules. Air Canada’s chatbot told a grieving passenger he could claim a bereavement discount after he flew. The real policy said no, and he had to take the airline to a tribunal to collect $812 (Canadian). Check the airline’s own policy page, and screenshot what the bot tells you.

Industry observers note that don’t click on the deal of the century. Scammers now use AI to make fake shopping sites look legitimate, and the number of fake sites jumped 250% last holiday season, according to NordVPN. Type the retailer’s address yourself.

Recent findings suggest that don’t try to win the family argument with AI-fetched facts. Even the creator of Angry Uncle Bot states that bombarding your uncle with facts only makes him angrier. Ask questions and listen instead.

Here’s another option: give technology a rest.

Unplug from your devices and from AI, and have an AI-free, 100% human Thanksgiving.
